page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration consists of 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, providing dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% with a stress-ng single-core value of 2865.09. However, its multi-core CPU performance falls into the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 11559.23. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, yielding 46.79 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 32.75 GB/sec for large block write operations. Other metrics, including Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU, consistently place this instance in the middle 50% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC hardware provides stable compute resources without the performance variability of shared-core instances, though the lack of bundled local storage requires provisioning external block storage. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance suitable for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale database operations. It is also capable of handling light language model inference, achieving an average prompt processing speed of 499.45 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.
